issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court may set aside a quasi-judicial cancellation of an allotment when the required finding of fraud is unsupported by evidence and rests on an incomplete consideration of the relevant material.
material_facts: The Chief Settlement Commissioner cancelled an allotment after concluding that the extracts supporting its grant were not genuine.

The original land records were unavailable, and the Commissioner relied on records from earlier years without addressing reports from revenue officials concerning the poor condition of the land and the risk of river erosion.
The Commissioner’s order identified no evidence supporting the conclusion that the extracts were not genuine.
The High Court found no evidence supporting the fraud finding and set aside the cancellation order.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to set aside the cancellation order because the Chief Settlement Commissioner’s finding of fraud was unsupported by evidence; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 empowers the Chief Settlement Commissioner to cancel an allotment obtained by fraud, false representation, or concealment of a material fact. The Commissioner’s satisfaction on that matter is a jurisdictional fact, not a conclusive determination. Because the power is judicial in character, a superior authority or a High Court exercising writ jurisdiction may examine whether the satisfaction was based on material and whether the order was arbitrary, capricious, or perverse. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: writ_review_of_allotment_cancellation and original_records_unavailable and relevant_reports_ignored and fraud_finding_unsupported

predicates.writ_review_of_allotment_cancellation: A party sought review in writ proceedings of an authority’s order cancelling an allotment.
predicates.original_records_unavailable: The decision-maker did not have the original records relevant to the alleged fraud.
predicates.relevant_reports_ignored: The decision-maker did not consider reports relevant to whether the allotment had been obtained by fraud.
predicates.fraud_finding_unsupported: The decision-maker’s finding of fraud had no evidentiary support in the material considered.

issues.definition: When an allotment cancellation is reviewed in writ proceedings, the cancellation is invalid if the original records are unavailable, relevant reports are ignored, and the fraud finding is unsupported.
